title: Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screens define the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response - Nature Biotechnology
text:
AbstractTo elucidate the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response (DDR) network, we conduct unbiased genetic interaction screens using Cas12a. We disrupt 233 DDR genes frequently mutated in cancer and other genetic diseases, either individually or in pairwise combinations, enabling us to assess the phenotypic effects induced by the loss of DDR gene pairs under unperturbed cell growth conditions. We identify high-confidence positive and negative gene–gene interactions, along with connections between previously unlinked DDR pathways. Among the identified genetic interactions, we uncover synthetic lethal interactions between genes encoding the translesion polymerase REV1–Pol ζ complex and the MCM8–MCM9–HROB DNA helicase complex, between Fanconi anemia genes and various mitotic DNA repair genes, as well as between genes encoding the DNA translocase SMARCAL1 and components of the FANCM complex, suggesting opportunities for targeted treatments in tumors carrying mutations in these genes. Collectively, our genetic map of the DDR network identifies synthetic lethal and buffering interactions with therapeutic potential.

Data availability

All screening data, as well as AlphaFold datasets for the prediction of physical interactions across all integrated datasets, are provided in the Supplementary Information and can be additionally requested on a dedicated website (https://ddr-genetic-interactions.ciccialab-database.com/). All unique reagents generated in this study will be made available upon request. Raw sequencing data and processed data tables containing gRNA counts for MCF10A and RPE-1 CRISPR–Cas12a pooled screens were deposited to the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) under accession number GSE343308. END-seq raw sequencing data and processed bigWig files are also available from the GEO under accession number GSE343490. Source data are provided with this paper.
